questions.prompt: The original source of new alleles in a population is…
questions.explanation: Mutations are random changes in DNA that create new alleles.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes natural selection?

choices.text: Individuals change during their lifetime to suit the environment
Better-adapted individuals survive and reproduce more, passing on their alleles
All individuals in a population are identical
Organisms choose which features to pass on

questions.explanation: Selection acts on existing variation; populations, not individuals, evolve.

questions.prompt: Finishing a full course of antibiotics helps reduce the spread of antibiotic resistance.
questions.explanation: It kills more of the bacteria, leaving fewer partly resistant survivors to multiply.

questions.prompt: Select **all** that count as evidence for evolution.
questions.explanation: Fossils, comparative anatomy and DNA all support evolution.

questions.prompt: Explain how a population of bacteria becomes resistant to an antibiotic.
questions.marking_guide: 1: variation exists — some bacteria have a resistance allele (from mutation). 1: antibiotic kills non-resistant bacteria (selection pressure). 1: resistant bacteria survive and reproduce. 1: allele passed on; frequency of resistance increases over generations.
questions.explanation: Variation → selection pressure → survival and reproduction of resistant bacteria → inheritance and increase in allele frequency.
